items.stem: A sound content strategy starts by defining:

options.text: How many posts to publish each week
options.rationale: Volume is an output decision, not the starting point.

options.text: Who the audience is and what business goal the content serves
options.rationale: Correct: audience and purpose anchor every later content decision.

options.text: Which colours to use in graphics
options.rationale: Visual choices follow strategy, not the other way round.
Competitor channels are input, not the foundation of your strategy.

items.explanation: Correct: audience and purpose anchor every later content decision.

options.text: Deleting old content to start fresh
options.rationale: Atomisation reuses content; it does not delete it.

options.text: Breaking one substantial piece into many smaller formats for different channels
options.rationale: Correct: a pillar piece is broken down and reshaped for multiple channels.

options.text: Writing every piece completely from scratch
options.rationale: That is the opposite of repurposing.

options.text: Publishing the same article on ten sites verbatim
options.rationale: Duplicating verbatim risks duplicate-content issues and is not atomisation.

items.explanation: Correct: a pillar piece is broken down and reshaped for multiple channels.

items.stem: Which TWO are meaningful content metrics tied to goals rather than vanity? (Select TWO)

options.text: Conversions or leads generated from a piece
options.rationale: Correct: conversions tie content directly to a business goal.

options.text: Engaged time or scroll depth on a page
options.rationale: Correct: engagement depth indicates whether content actually held attention.

options.text: Raw page views with no context
options.rationale: Unqualified views are a classic vanity metric.

options.text: Number of words published this month
options.rationale: Word count measures effort, not value delivered.

items.explanation: Correct: conversions tie content directly to a business goal.; Correct: engagement depth indicates whether content actually held attention.
